detail.heading: DNS zone
detail.subtitle: The records this server answers with for the name, and how to point the name here.
detail.notFoundDescription: This zone does not exist, or it belongs to another account.

zones.heading: DNS zones
zones.subtitle: The domain names this server answers DNS queries for.
zones.emptyDescription: Create a zone to publish the DNS records of a domain from this server.
zones.noResultsDescription: Change the search or the filters, or clear them to see every zone.
zones.confirmDelete: Every record in the zone is deleted and this server stops answering for the name. The domain stops resolving here until a zone is created again.
zones.confirmDeleteSigned: Every record in the zone is deleted and this server stops answering for the name. This zone is signed: remove the DS record at your registrar first, because a DS record that stays published for a zone that is no longer signed makes validating resolvers reject the name, and the domain stops resolving for them.

templates.heading: Zone templates
templates.subtitle: The records a new zone starts with. Built-in templates can be changed but not deleted.
templates.emptyDescription: Create a template to give new zones a set of records to start from.
templates.madeDefault: The template {name} is now the default.
templates.noResultsDescription: Change the search or clear it to see every template.
templates.confirmDelete: Zones already created from it keep their records. New zones can no longer start from it.

form.subtitle: A template is a named set of records. The server checks every record and every variable when you save.

placeholders.name: Web and mail

records.valueHint: The value can use the variables listed below the form.

variables.heading: Variables
variables.subtitle: Written in a value, a variable is replaced with the real figure when a zone is created.

zoneForm.heading: New zone

hints.template: A template adds its records to the new zone. Choose an empty zone to add them yourself.

errors.accountRequired: Choose the account that owns the zone.
errors.nameRequired: Enter the domain name of the zone.
errors.nameInvalid: Enter a domain name of two or more parts, such as example.com.

records.emptyDescription: Add a record to publish an address, a mail server or any other data for this zone.
records.noResultsDescription: Change the search or the filters, or clear them to see every record.
records.confirmDelete: The name server stops answering with this record as soon as the zone is applied.

placeholders.name: {'@'} for the zone itself, or www

errors.nameRequired: Enter a name. Use {'@'} for the zone itself.
errors.nameInvalid: Use letters, digits, hyphens and underscores in dot-separated parts. A * may stand alone as the first part.
errors.ttlInvalid: Enter the TTL as a whole number of seconds.
errors.ttlRange: The TTL must be between {min} and {max} seconds.
errors.numberRange: Enter a whole number from 0 to {max}.
errors.tagInvalid: Choose one of the listed tags.
errors.valueControl: A value cannot contain line breaks or other control characters.
errors.valueTooLong: A value can be up to {max} characters long.

nameservers.heading: Nameservers
nameservers.subtitle: The name server on this host and the values written into every zone it serves.
nameservers.settingsSubtitle: Written into the SOA and the NS set of every zone.

hints.nameservers: One host name per line, such as ns1.example.com. Create glue records for them at the registrar of their domain.
hints.hostmaster: The contact address of the zones, written the way the SOA record writes it: a dot instead of the at sign, so hostmaster.example.com stands for hostmaster{'@'}example.com.
hints.rerender: Saving writes the new values into every zone on this server.

errors.nameserverInvalid: A name server must be a host name such as ns1.example.net.
errors.hostmasterInvalid: Write the mailbox with a dot instead of the at sign, such as hostmaster.example.com.
errors.ipv4Invalid: Enter an IPv4 address such as 203.0.113.10.
errors.ipv6Invalid: Enter an IPv6 address such as 2001:db8::10.

nameservers.incomplete: The settings are incomplete, so zones cannot be created yet. Fill in the primary name server and the hostmaster mailbox, then save.

server.heading: Name server
server.onExplanation: This server answers DNS queries on port {port} for the zones it holds, to whoever the firewall lets reach it.
server.offExplanation: This server does not answer DNS queries. Zones are kept.
server.turnedOn: The name server was turned on.
server.turnedOff: The name server was turned off.
server.confirmOn: This starts the name server, which listens on every address of this server. It does not open port {port} in the firewall: if the panel firewall does not let the port through, nobody outside can query it, and if no firewall is running the port is reachable at once. Domains start resolving here once their registrars delegate them to this server.
server.confirmOff: This stops the name server. Every zone stops resolving from this server, and the zones are kept. Any firewall rule for port {port} stays until you remove it.
server.agentUnreachable: The panel could not reach the agent on this host, so the state below is what the panel last stored.

firewall.label: Port {port} in the panel firewall
firewall.blocked: The name server is turned on, but no panel firewall rule lets TCP and UDP port {port} through. Turning the server on does not open the port, so nobody outside this server can query it if the panel firewall is in force.
firewall.lingering: The name server is turned off and the panel firewall still lets port {port} through. Turning the server off does not close the port.

descriptions.off: This zone is served unsigned. DNSSEC lets resolvers check that the answers for this name were not altered on the way.
descriptions.signing: This zone is served signed. Validating resolvers only trust it once the DS record below is published at your registrar.
descriptions.withdrawing: This zone is served unsigned while the signing is withdrawn. The DS record must be removed at your registrar before the withdrawal can be finished.

dnssec.noRollover: There is no automatic key rollover. This panel uses one signing key and never replaces it by itself. To use a new key, withdraw the signing and enable it again, and publish the new DS record at the registrar.

observed.publishedKey: Key published by the name server
observed.publishedKeyTag: Key tag published by the name server

reports.notInForce: Not confirmed by the name server

registrar.title: Publish the DS record at your registrar
registrar.instructions: Open the DNS or DNSSEC settings of this domain at your registrar and add a DS record with the four fields below. Some registrars ask for the DNSKEY instead; its fields follow the DS record. The panel cannot publish it for you. Until the registrar publishes it, resolvers treat the zone as unsigned.
registrar.removeTitle: Remove the DS record at your registrar
registrar.removeInstructions: Open the DNS or DNSSEC settings of this domain at your registrar and delete the DS record shown below. Do this first, and wait until the registrar has published its removal. Removing it last leaves a DS record for a zone that is not signed, and validating resolvers then reject the name.

ds.title: DS record
ds.subtitle: Enter these four values at the registrar.

dnskey.title: DNSKEY
dnskey.subtitle: For registrars that ask for the public key instead of the DS record.

enable.title: Sign this zone
enable.subtitle: The panel generates a signing key and the name server starts serving the zone signed.
enable.confirm: The panel generates a signing key and this server serves the zone signed. Then publish the DS record at your registrar. A DS record that does not match the zone's key makes validating resolvers reject the name, and the domain stops resolving for them.

withdraw.title: Withdraw DNSSEC
withdraw.subtitle: Stops signing the zone. Remove the DS record at your registrar first.
withdraw.confirm: Remove the DS record at your registrar first, never last. If the DS record is still published once the zone is served unsigned, validating resolvers reject the name and the domain stops resolving for them. The zone is served unsigned from now on, and the withdrawal can be finished after a waiting period.

finish.title: Finish the withdrawal
finish.subtitle: Deletes the signing key. Available after a waiting period, once the DS record is gone from the registrar.
finish.earliest: The withdrawal can be finished from {when}.
finish.dsRemoved: I removed the DS record at the registrar
finish.confirm: The signing key is deleted for good. If the DS record is still published at the registrar, validating resolvers reject the name and the domain stops resolving for them. Confirm only if you removed the DS record at the registrar first.
